children: Canada's main index gave back some of its monthly gain on Monday, weighed by declines for industrial and metal mining shares, as investors took  some profits ahead of a seasonally weak period for the market.
ended down 283.44 points, or 0.8%, at 36,270.48, its lowest closing level since August 6. Still, the index posted a monthly advance of nearly 3%, which was its fifth straight monthly gain.
"Investors may be taking profit ahead of the month of September," said Sid Mokhtari, chief market technician for CIBC Capital Markets. "It's a month not to be too complacent."
September has historically proved to be the worst month for the U.S. stock market.
U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish tone in a speech on Friday at the Jackson Hole Symposium has also contributed to investor caution, Mokhtari said.

Investors expect the Bank of Canada to leave its benchmark interest rate on hold at 2.25% on Wednesday as the recent increase in trade tensions between the United States and Canada offsets stronger economic growth in the second quarter than the central bank expected. (0#CADIRPR)
